transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Yeah, um, so, I'm here because... well, honestly, I'm just having a really, really hard time getting anything done lately. The main thing is I just get pulled off track by every single little sound or thought that pops into my head. Like, I’ll sit down at my desk, right? And I'll tell myself I'm going to work on a job application—because I've been trying to find work for a while now, and since I only have my high school diploma it's already kind of tough out there, so I really need to focus—but anyway, I'll be staring at the application on my screen, and then a car will drive by outside. And it's not even a loud car, just like regular street traffic, but suddenly I'm looking out the window, wondering where they're going or what kind of engine it has. Or my phone screen will light up, not even a text, just like a random spam email notification, and I'll pick it up. Or I'll just have some completely random idea, like, I don't know, 'I wonder what happened to that guy I did a group project with in tenth grade,' and it just sends me somewhere else entirely. And the craziest part is, I do all this before I even notice I'm doing it. Like, an hour will go by and I'll be deep into some internet rabbit hole, and I'll suddenly realize the job application is just sitting there completely blank. It's incredibly frustrating because it happens all day, every day, with literally everything I try to do, and I just can't seem to stop it from happening.
Do you also tend to feel physically restless or fidgety, like you have trouble sitting still?

Oh, yeah, absolutely. Like, 100%. It's actually kind of funny you ask that, because my mom used to yell at me about it all the time when I was a kid, and honestly, it hasn't really stopped. Even now, if I'm sitting down talking to someone—like, if I'm at a coffee shop with a friend, or even just sitting here talking to you—my leg is almost always bouncing up and down. It's like this nervous energy that just has to go somewhere, you know? And if it's not my leg, it's my hands. I'm always clicking a pen if I have one, like, click-click-click, until someone finally glares at me and asks me to stop. Or I'll be digging in my pocket and just messing with my keys, flipping them around over and over. The weirdest part is, I don't even realize I'm doing it most of the time. It's completely unconscious. Like, someone will point it out, and I'll look down at my hands or my leg and be like, 'Oh, wow, I didn't even know that was happening.' It's just this constant need to be moving some part of my body, even if it's just a tiny little movement, because sitting completely still just feels... I don't know, almost physically uncomfortable. Like my skin is crawling if I don't move.
Were these attention and restlessness problems already present before you were 7 years old?

Yeah, oh man, definitely. It goes way back. I mean, my mom says I was always like this, even when I was really little, but I definitely remember it being a huge issue in elementary school. It was always a whole thing. I remember in first grade, second grade, third grade—pretty much every single year, honestly—the teachers were always moving my desk. Like, they'd start me out in the middle of the room with everyone else, but by the second week of school, my desk would be pushed right up against the teacher's desk, or like, isolated in a corner by the chalkboard. And it was because I just couldn't keep quiet. I was always talking out of turn, blurting out answers before they even finished asking the question, or just leaning over to talk to whoever was sitting next to me about whatever random thing popped into my head. 

And the schoolwork itself was a total disaster. I was constantly forgetting my homework. Like, I'd actually do it at home sometimes—well, if my mom sat there and forced me to—and then I'd just leave it on the kitchen table. Or I'd shove it in my backpack and it would get crumpled into this little ball at the bottom, and I wouldn't be able to find it when the teacher asked for it. And when we had to do worksheets in class, I would just rush through them so fast. I just wanted to be done, you know? So I wouldn't even read the instructions properly. I'd skip whole sections, or add numbers instead of subtracting them, just making these really dumb, careless mistakes all over the place. My teachers were always writing notes in red pen like, "Slow down!" or "Check your work!" but I just couldn't. It felt like my brain was going a million miles an hour and my pencil was just trying to keep up. So yeah, this isn't new at all. It's basically been the story of my life since I was a little kid.
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, much more than your normal self?

No, I... I don't think so. Like, unusually energized? Not really in the way you're describing, I don't think. I mean, I have that restless, bouncing-off-the-walls energy all the time, right? Like I was just saying with the leg bouncing and the pen clicking and all that. That's just my normal baseline. But like, a period of days where I feel euphoric or super energized? No, definitely not. If anything, I'm usually just exhausted from trying to keep my brain on track all day. It's like, by the time the evening rolls around, I'm just totally drained from fighting with myself to get even one simple thing done, like that job application. I'll just sit on the couch and be like, 'Man, I have no energy left.' So, yeah, I've never had a time where I felt like I had some kind of superpower energy or felt on top of the world for days on end. It's pretty much just the constant, annoying fidgety energy, but mentally I'm just... tired. Always just kind of tired and frustrated with myself. So, no, nothing like what you're asking about, not at all.
When you were a child, did you often blurt out answers before the question was finished?

Yeah, exactly like I was saying about elementary school earlier! It was a huge problem then, but the thing is, it never really stopped. Even now, I cut people off a lot. Like, all the time. It happens especially with my mom, or when I'm talking to my counselor, because an answer just pops into my head and I say it before they’re even done talking. 

I'll be sitting there, and my mom will be halfway through a sentence about, I don't know, what we're doing for dinner or asking me about something around the house, and the exact second I know where she's going with it—boom, the words are already out of my mouth. It's like my brain just completely skips the part where you're supposed to politely wait your turn. I really don't mean to be rude, you know? It's just that the thought is right there, and it feels like if I don't say it that exact second, it's either going to disappear completely from my brain, or I'm just going to physically explode trying to hold it in. 

My counselor gets it a lot, too. We'll be in the middle of a session, and she'll be trying to make a really good point or ask me a question, and I just bulldoze right over her. She's always having to stop and hold up her hand and be like, "Hold on, let me finish," and then I feel terrible about it because I realize I did it again. But in the moment, I don't even think. It's just a reflex. The answer is just sitting right on my tongue, and I spit it out before the other person has even gotten to the question mark at the end of their sentence. So yeah, I definitely did it as a kid, but it's still a massive thing for me now.
